claim: suggested_pricing.reasoning: "The monthly fee is 40-60% above the cheapest AI competitor on purpose"
problem: Arithmetic is contradicted by the plan's own competitor prices. $550/month is about 5.5x Klugon's $99 entry tier, and only about 10-22% above VetRec Plus ($499), Klugon Scale ($499) and 24PetLine Growth ($449). No cited competitor price produces a 40-60% gap ($344-$393/month).
fix: Restate the positioning with figures that reconcile: "about 10-20% above the $449-$499 tiers from 24PetLine/VetRec and roughly 1.8x Klugon's $299 Business tier, but ~5.5x its $99 entry tier", or drop the percentage entirely.

claim: Integrations: on-call technician transfer cost = "Included in the per-minute agent rate; no separate transfer fee published"
problem: Retell's own call-transfer docs say the agent charge stops once the agent leaves the call, but telephony charges continue for the transferred leg at the destination's per-minute rate (~$0.015/min). So the transfer is not fully inside the per-minute agent rate - the plan's wording implies the handoff is free.
fix: Reword to: "No separate transfer fee; agent billing stops at handoff and telephony continues at $0.015/min for the remaining transferred call".

claim: feasibility.weeks_to_pilot: "6 (4 weeks of build and simulation after a 1-week baseline, plus 1 week of schedule buffer)", then a 4-week pilot
problem: Internally inconsistent. Six weeks to pilot start would put go-live in week 7, but the build plan schedules the pilot as "weeks 5-8" (phases 0-3 occupy weeks 1-4) and the review at week 9. Both cannot be true.
fix: Either drop the buffer and state 5 weeks to pilot with the pilot in weeks 5-8 and review in week 9, or move the pilot to weeks 7-10, week 11 review, and update every phase/week reference.

claim: Competitor Otto: "the plans page lists one price for the bundled platform but requires a quote request"
problem: The cited page contains no price at all (no $ figure anywhere in the rendered page); "one price" there is marketing copy about a single bundled offering, not a listed price. As written the sentence implies a published fixed price.
fix: Change to: "No price published on the plans page; only a quote request form."

claim: Competitor PetDesk: "U.S. pricing for Vetstoria (which operates as PetDesk in the U.S.) is directed to PetDesk for a quote", cited to petdesk.com/frequently-asked-questions
problem: The cited FAQ supports only "pricing depends on what you want - contact sales" and does not mention Vetstoria at all. The corporate relationship is the reverse of the wording: PetDesk acquired Vetstoria and markets the booking product as PetDesk Booking (formerly Vetstoria).
fix: Keep the FAQ for the quote-only point, and either drop the Vetstoria sentence or cite a page that shows the acquisition/rebranding (e.g. a PetDesk Booking description) and describe PetDesk as the owner of Vetstoria's booking product.

claim: Leverage / integrations: "AVImark has no self-serve public API and requires Covetrus partner approval", cited to dataservices.idexx.com/documentation/Cornerstone
problem: The source is right for IDEXX but cannot support an AVImark claim; the AVImark statement is sourced to an IDEXX page. The underlying claim does check out against Covetrus's own partner/integration pages (application + agreement, no public docs), so this is a citation error, not a false claim.
fix: Cite the Covetrus technology-integration/partner page for the AVImark point and keep the IDEXX URL only for Cornerstone Data Services.

claim: problem.summary: the building is "staffed ... by roughly a dozen people"
problem: Not supported by any cited page. The team page now carries no staff roster, so the headcount is an unlabeled inference.
fix: Either drop the headcount or mark it as an inference carried from profile research with its basis stated.

claim: Integration cost: "WordPress core REST API is free" cited to developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/
problem: The handbook documents the API but states no price; "$0" is inference/general knowledge rather than something the cited page shows. Low materiality (core WordPress is free software), but the citation does not carry the cost claim.
fix: Label the $0 as inference (no per-call licence on core REST API) or cite the WordPress core licence/pricing page instead.
